title: Status Reviews of Long Holds: Training Notes on Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
These training notes set out, as questions answered, the rule for status reviews of running holds under Hardship and Protective Holds.

## The rule

Tiers whose review interval is above 0 are reviewed while they run: the first review falls due the tier's review interval in calendar days after the start date, and each later review the same number of days after the previous due date. Reviews are recorded only on a hold whose status is active. A review records *continue hold* when the qualifying condition still holds on the consumer's updated documentation, and *end hold* otherwise, which ends the hold that day with the end reason *review not continued*. A review not recorded within the tier's review overdue days, in calendar days, after it fell due ends the hold with the end reason *review not continued* on the first day after that period. A review never shortens or lengthens the end date.

## Questions answered

**Which holds are reviewed?** Only tiers whose review interval is above 0 — the Long-Term Hardship Hold and the Military Service Hold. A tier with an interval of 0 has no reviews.

**When does each review fall due?** The first falls due one review interval after the start date; each later one falls due one review interval after the previous due date.

**On what is a review decided?** On the consumer's updated documentation: if the qualifying condition still holds, the review records continue hold; otherwise it records end hold.

**What does an end-hold outcome do?** It ends the hold that same day, with the end reason review not continued.

**What if a review is not recorded at all?** If no review is recorded within the overdue days after it fell due, the hold ends with the end reason review not continued on the first day after that period.

**Can a review be recorded on an undecided request or an ended hold?** No. Reviews are recorded only on a hold whose status is active.

**Does a review move the end date?** No. A review never shortens or lengthens the end date.

## Worked dates (hypothetical)

A Long-Term Hardship Hold (review interval 60 calendar days, overdue days 15) starts on 1 March.

| Item | Date |
|---|---|
| First review falls due (60 days after 1 March) | 30 April |
| Last day of its overdue period (15 days after 30 April) | 15 May |
| Hold ends if that review is still unrecorded | 16 May, end reason review not continued |
| Second review falls due (60 days after 30 April) | 29 June |

If the first review is recorded on 10 May as continue hold, the hold runs on and its end date is unchanged. If it is recorded on 10 May as end hold, the hold ends on 10 May.
